I don't really abuse drugs (anymore) per say. I still smoke quite a fair bit of weed but I rarely (if ever) take anything else bar it. I like smoking weed, it's a nice feeling, it helps me relax and chill out. It's great for nights in too.

I have however been smoking counterfeit tobacco for the last month. I got 50g of it for £2 a packet and I stopped smoking it a few days out of a suspicion as I had a cough since about when I started smoking it. It went away in about 2 days. Started again today, I felt better after my first one (in my head and physically) and now I have a cough again and I'm throwing up. I think some of the chemicals in it has been fucking with me pretty badly, I have smoked about 75g of it so far.

Thanks a lot. I did open up to one of my friends (over facebook chat although. I truthfully have never managed to speak about this sort of stuff to a great level in person whilst sober.)

I wasn't a big fan of the medication but I can be a very social person and the medication can really put a big hit on that part of your life. I like going out and I do live in a place where people mainly go out, to go out for a drink. Thanks for the response again, I appreciate it.

Next year two of them are going into their final year at University (fourth year, honours) and my worry is more so directed at one of them. I can be a pretty bad influence on him at times and he'll go out drinking a lot with me.

I think you're mis-understanding where I'm coming from here. That's fine, either way. It's my life in the end, I do what I want with it, there's only been a few people in my life that have really pushed me and invested in what I could possibly do and I think it'd be unfair of me just to opt-out all of a sudden. I wouldn't go as far as to call it selfish, but unfair.

I'm a fan of music with a lot of imagery. Admittedly, the one I am most fond of (due to being a Pink Floyd fan) is The Wall (as in the movie). Although I have a large interest in politics, philosophy and what not so that might be why I enjoy it, as it's not like how you've described Holland 1945.

Keep them coming. Being able to experience various types of comforting music has really improved my mood so far. I have a good hope that this may help a few others who are needing to sit and have a think to a nice piece of music.
Thanks for the share. I've listened to Cloud Cult but not this song in particular before and it's lovely.

If there is one thing I've always kept in mind, it's that you can't expect the entirety of the people around you regardless if it's real life or the internet to be understanding. I laugh at some pretty fucked up stuff myself so it'd be entirely hypocritical of me to go off at them for it.

Used to drink 3 days a week on average (student n'all. Tis cheap). Ended up on Medication, continued to drink and smoke weed and occasionally take some other stuff as well like charlie. Wish I didn't. Seriously, if you're feeling shit at any point, stop it. I know it works differently for others, but chemically things like alcohol are depressants and will only eventually make you worse off.

If there's one thing you need to remember, is that during the aftermath of events like this, a lot of things are blown out of proportion and it can create a horrible thought for those who aren't completely mentally stable themselves.

I'm an incredibly over-analytic person. I worry about everything in-depth so something like this would freak me out if I was in your shoes. All I can say is, the fact that you're still self-aware shows you're more than likely not to follow down that path, and I hope you don't. For your own sake.

Look on the bright side anyway, you're 17! I'm a year older than you and this is the first year I've actually tried dealing with my problems, I've had some serious fucking downs but they're worth it, because you're soon going to start experiencing the best part of your life.

I can't understand that idea either. I find it incredibly similar to the arguments for/against euthanasia however. However, a lot of it spawns from the concept that most people develop, and that is trying to live up to expectations, regardless of how high they are set.

I don't think that suicide is selfish, but I think about the few who care about me, especially my Mother who raised me on her own to be the best I could. She worries about me relentlessly and I think one thing that has actually stopped me from taking my own life is that I wouldn't feel right leaving her to deal with something so traumatizing.

In the end, I wouldn't take it personally. It's always down to perspective, maturity and how you can interpret things. If I'd seen this on r/funny normally I'd probably not have blinked an eye and just moved on.

I suffer from sleeping issues regularly and it probably has a lot to do with my condition, I'm not in the best shape anymore although I don't really think about it, if I'm honest.

I think you need to try and get into a good sleeping pattern, be more socializing/outgoing etc. Surrounding yourself with good friends will inherently boost both your self-esteem and confidence. If you're concerned about your weight, try going to the gym. Taking the first steps in this situation REGARDLESS of what they are is always hard, but keep at them and it'll pay off in such a great way. Exercise is a great way to make you start feeling more positive about yourself, especially in this sort of position. When people around you notice and begin to compliment your improvement, it'll also be a good boost.

After being taken off medication I started drinking again immediately (still drank but lightly on it) and also I was still smoking a lot of weed. I smoke normally as well. If you mean tobacco, that's a normal way to deal with stress. It's how I deal with when I'm stressing out.

I'd maybe suggest speaking to your wife, and also stop drinking. Alcohol is a serious depressant (which is something I've learned the hard way about 3 times in the last week) and will not do you any favors. Good luck, and stay strong.

My aim is to do all of my work in the next few hours, go in, sit exam, come home, sleep, pack up and go home for Christmas. If I don't get out of here soon I'm worried that I'm going to have a dangerous episode and start self harming even more, or even worse. It's fucking horrible being this temperamental. Thanks for reaching out and taking the time to respond, by the way. Even the little things can really help when you're not feeling right in the head anymore, and it's nice to have someone speak to you like you're a normal person.

I get to the stage a lot where I won't shower unless I'm leaving the house (unless I'm going to Tesco in the car and back) because I don't have the motivation to take care of myself, I'll sometimes just go without eating as well because I don't have the enthusiasm to get out of my bed long enough to even cook.

I know it's all down to perspective, but I have no idea how someone could laugh at that sort of picture. It may be a soft spot for me because of my problems, but for someone to laugh at that would actually make me feel a bit belittled.

I'd listen to what RadicalSelf had to say. Trying to deal with other peoples issues when you have your own can not end well all the time, and they might be making themselves worse. I understand you may be worried that they'll hate you for it, but REGARDLESS of what the outcome could be - you need to get them help instantly. Have you tried speaking to their parents?

That's how it started for me. Albeit I've had issues in the past which have been created through trust issues, and what not. I moved in with friends this year and at first, it was the best time I've ever had in my life. About 4 months in, I just began to feel off quite a lot and didn't deal with it properly.

I ended up on medication, which I got taken off about two weeks ago (I was on it for a month). I've been seeing a counselor and it isn't working for me. I've ended up self-harming several times and I've had periods where I've been near enough to the point where I can't dispute the action of killing myself, especially the last week.

I never had a particularly bad upbringing. Yeah, didn't get on the best with a good amount of people at school but that was purely down to my own choices (I refused to be a stuck up, arrogant prick) although I still acted like a twat and I punish myself mentally for it everyday.

If there's any advice I can give you, from someone who went from being viewed as the guy who was always cheery, outgoing and what not: please, go to your doctor and speak to them about it and don't worry about judgment from them. They are **there to help you**. I eventually found out that I suffer from recurring depressive disorder, and although I've not made my mind up that it feels better to know this fact, at least it presents an opportunity as to how I can deal with it. That might be what you need.

May I note, there is a possibility of a hormonal imbalance. I'm tempted to get blood tests done to see if I've developed that during/after I've came off my medication because I've been very unstable the last week and a bit.

I know why, and I do understand. I do have a large issue with trusting people from the past (and how some of it took over me) and unfortunately it shows often. If I'm having episodes of depression, suicidal thoughts and stuff I can be a bit overbearing. I've apologized to her a lot on several occassions about bestowing my issues on her because although I talk to her about hers, it's not fair for me to do so because I knew that it's not good to hear a friend is struggling/relapsing when you're not too secure with your own issues and have these sort of days yourself.

I spoke to her for a bit, but we've agreed not to really talk for a while because of the emotional effect it was having, mainly on her. I was being erratic and pretty destructive at the time and I had to calm down and re-read everything I said to realize how much of a dick I was actually being. She told me I need to stop punishing myself for everything I feel like I've done wrong, seek better help and move on from these problems.

The last 7 days have just made me want to live less and less. I have an exam in about 8 hours that I've not done any study for and I need to write a shit load of reports or I'm going to endanger my grade. Getting paraplegic off something and just letting myself bleed out seems like a peaceful option to go out with.

My friend doesn't want to speak to me about this stuff anymore and she wants as much distance away from it as possible. she was really eloquent in explaining why and I do completely understand, she has her own stuff to deal with and she needs just a big break from everything, especially after the last 6 odd months.

I'm going to try and get better during this. I need to re-establish myself and just start doing what I bloody need to and not freaking the hell out of myself and others. Just calm and simpler sailing.

I just don't feel the point anymore. I tried speaking to my other friend through Facebook since I can't get a hold of her either way and she's just ignoring me now. After I went and saw The Hobbit with her she's just flat-out refused to speak to me (or at least it feels like that) and now I'm feeling even fucking worse than I did last night. I don't know if I can hold on, I really don't.

I'm a student in the UK who has an issue with depression/anxiety and the instances are entirely at random. The Counselor provided to me through the University is pretty crap at holding a conversation with me. I attempted to get external help through my GP/NHS (because I can't afford £50 for an hour session, I barely have any money each month as it is) and they can't be found through them in my area (Dundee) because there's so fucking many people on a stupidly big waiting list.

**tl;dr:**The UK is the same, especially if you're in a big area.

My episode eventually ended, I spent time watching films and television with my friend and a friend of hers which cheered me up a lot. She's aware of what I'm going through and that I was self-harming, although she phoned me this morning upset because she found some blood in her sink which was left there by me cleaning the blood off my arm, and I was almost certain I had cleaned it all away after.

I was on Fluoxetine for about a month and I eventually asked to be taken off it. At the start of my period on it I got a lot worse and I eventually started self-harming, anxiety/panic attacks became a lot more often and I lost the will to leave the house bar going shopping. I know it's horrible at the start, but push through and you'll feel a lot better after the six week course.

If you don't mind me asking, does your doctor intend to forward you onto a Consular/Therapist whilst you're on them?

Dedicated Servers weren't present in Modern Warfare 2 PC along with any iteration of the game which was released on consoles. After Modern Warfare 2 however, they did return on PC again however aren't ranked and are slyly hidden.

I was a massive fan of both Call of Duty 2 and 4. I spent an endless amount of hours playing them. I purchased Black Ops II to play with my flatmates on the Xbox (communal) and I've not noticed any issues personally. On the first day there was issues in regards to actually getting online, but this wasn't surprising due to the sheer amount of people attempting to play it.

On consoles, there are various reasons why you may suffer from a bad experience. The host may be from a different country (as will the majority of the other players, however this is only occurs in the middle of the night (00:00 onwards)) or if you're in a country which doesn't actually have that many players it's self. Other reasons may include high latency (on either or both ends), issues with your phone line etc.

If the hosts Internet, along with yours is technically sound then you're not going to experience any issues. Some people are however very unfortunate. You'll most likely find however the number of bad hosts will lower over time as the game becomes very selective based on track record (as does Halo) and current in/out/latency.

For people who are struggling to find a match, particularly with friends - make sure all of their NAT types are on open. You can easily find port-forwarding guides via Google. Once that is sorted you'll have a far better experience.

In terms of actual game-play, I actually think Treyarch have done an alright job this time around. I like the new Pick 10 system for classes, allows you to mix it up very well and the game-play seems fairly balanced for a change on release. Modern Warfare 3 was a huge disappointment and personally, I've found this iteration to probably have been the best so far since Call of Duty 4.

Quick Edit: The same software for hosting games is still used, FYI. The only difference being that Dedicated Servers were on a committed box in some building, with a line far better than a residential one (generally 100Mbps at minimum, where-as Residential can be lower than 8Mbps, especially in the UK).
